terms.meaning: Sending news or information from one person or place to another.
Creating and spreading information with the help of technology.
Using the features of living things to make useful products with technology.
The washing away of the fertile top soil by wind, rain and floods.
Setting up factories and the transport and power they need.

items.name: Three kinds of mass media
items.example: Newspapers are called a record of the day's history.

items.name: First Kannada newspaper
items.example: Papers can be daily, weekly, monthly or annual.

items.name: Electronic media
items.formula: TV, radio, mobile and internet: news in seconds and early warnings of disasters.
items.example: Mobile reaches even people who can't read.

items.name: Commercial and art cinema
items.formula: Art (parallel) cinema studies a subject seriously and fights superstition.

items.name: Bengaluru and IT
items.formula: Called India's Silicon City; Infosys and Wipro lead in software.
items.example: Karnataka's IT plan came in 1997; the Cyber Park project began in 2000.

items.name: Dolly the sheep
items.formula: The world's first cloned sheep, by the scientist Wilmut in 1997.
items.example: Branches of biotechnology: tissue culture, DNA fingerprinting, cloning.

items.name: Biotechnology in Karnataka
items.formula: Biotech Parks at the Agriculture Universities of Bengaluru and Dharwad; a marine centre at Karwar.
items.example: Biocon is a leading private company.

items.name: Karnataka's land
items.formula: About 1,91,791 sq km; about 190.50 lakh hectares.

items.name: Why agriculture is the backbone
items.formula: It gives food, raw materials for industry, jobs and markets.
items.example: In 2011, 49% of Karnataka's people depended on farming.

items.name: Irrigation projects
items.formula: Tungabhadra, Upper Krishna, Bhadra, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Hemavati, Harangi and others.

items.name: Industries of Karnataka
items.formula: Iron and steel, aluminium, cotton, silk, sugar, paper, electronics and cement.
items.example: Gandhiji: cottage industries are lamps guiding a country to progress.

items.name: Industrial policies
items.formula: Central policies of 1948, 1956, 1977 and 1980; Karnataka's own in 1996 and 2001.

mistakes.text: IT works with information; biotechnology works with living things.
Karnataka's own industrial policy came in 1996; the earlier ones were the Central government's.
Soil erosion has human causes too, such as cutting forests and wrong farming.
